req.title: Task title trimmed of whitespace
req.statement: The system shall trim leading and trailing whitespace from the title on POST /tasks/.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-037 requires that POST /tasks/ trims leading and trailing whitespace from the task title. The test suite must verify: (1) positive case — a title with surrounding whitespace is accepted and stored trimmed; (2) negative case — a title that is only whitespace (becomes empty after trim) should be rejected; (3) boundary cases — single leading space, single trailing space, mixed internal whitespace (not trimmed), and titles at the max-length boundary after trimming. Each test asserts exact status codes and exact response field values to maximise mutation kill rate. The SUT source shows that schemas.TaskBase uses Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100) for title, and crud.create_task stores task.title directly — so trimming must happen at the schema/validation layer. We assert the exact trimmed value in the response body to catch mutations that skip or partially apply the strip operation.

tests.name: test_post_task_leading_trailing_whitespace_trimmed
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
actions: POST /tasks/ with title '   Buy groceries   ' (leading and trailing spaces)
trace: R-TASK-037: system shall trim leading and trailing whitespace from title on POST /tasks/
tests.executable:
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite://')
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app.database import Base, engine
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_task_leading_trailing_whitespace_trimmed():
    payload = {"title": "   Buy groceries   ", "completed": False}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["title"] == "Buy groceries"
    assert body["completed"] == False
    assert "id" in body

test_post_task_leading_trailing_whitespace_trimmed()
